All areas served

Make your interior work for you.

Interior renovation often starts with the way a space is used: a room needs more privacy, a route through the home no longer works, or a floor needs replacing. Création & Rénovation Gessienne approaches these projects through its masonry, plastering, partitioning and tiling trades, from its base in Gex across its French and Swiss service areas.

Prepare our first conversation

Rethink the layout.

Creating a separation, adjusting a room layout or working on a wall calls for a view of the whole home. Circulation, openings and elements to retain guide the discussion. A structural alteration differs from a simple partition change: the checks needed depend on the building and the project.

  • Masonry and wall repairs
  • Partitions and interior layouts

Prepare surfaces and junctions.

Plastering and lining work help prepare the space. Junctions with ceilings, retained walls and openings need to be examined to define the expected finish. Point out visible irregularities or defects: these need to be understood before the surface is covered.

  • Plastering and linings
  • Substrate preparation

Choose finishes in context.

Tiling is chosen in relation to the room, its use and its substrate. Format, thickness, laying direction and joints affect levels and junctions. Where several stages of work follow one another, their order is planned around the agreed scope. Work belonging to other trades must be identified separately; it is not automatically included in an interior renovation enquiry.

Before you begin.

What does your interior renovation work cover?

It is based on masonry, plastering, partitions and tiling. The exact scope is defined from your needs and an assessment of the property, then set out in the project documents.

Do I need to choose every material before getting in touch?

No. You can share your ideas and explain how you want to use the space. If you have already chosen a finish, give its reference, format and thickness to support the discussion about the substrate and installation.
